rename.from: Input with name "class" has a different behaviour in ng8 and ng9
rename.to: Input with name "class" and host binding for class have a different behaviour in ng8 and ng9

body:
See for explanation:
https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/389379918303391d07fb5b2a074bf8b00dc66e6b/packages/core/src/render3/instructions/styling.ts#L253-L267

This is expected/intended/correct behavior.

Assume you have your own component `<greet>` with property `name`
```
@Component({
  selector: `greet'
})
class GreetComponent {
  @Input('name')
  name: string;

  @Input('class')
  klass: string;
}
```

Therefore in this example: 
```
<greet name="World"></greet>
<greet [name]="expression"></greet>
```
In the above example both of the cases will assign to `name` property of `<greet>`. Therefore for consistency the following example should behave same.
```
<greet class="World"></greet> // CASE A
<greet [class]="expression"></greet>
```
So the fact that in View Engine case A does not work is a bug with VE as it is inconsistent with the rest of template syntax behavior. 

Finally in the last example
```
<greet class="World" [class]="expression"></greet>
```
one would expect that both values get concatenated before they are written to the property, which is exactly the behavior of Ivy.

Closing as working as intended.

# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package Not sure ### Is this a regression? Yes, the previous version in which this bug was not present was: 8.2.14 ### Description For example we have this component: ```ts import { Component, Input } from '@angular/core'; @Component({ selector: 'app-test', template: 'className is "{{ className }}" but should be undefined' }) export class TestComponent { @Input() className: string; } ``` If we use it like this: ```html ``` `TestComponent` will render `className is "foo" but should be undefined` which is not correct as `className` input was not provided. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction Couldn't reproduce it on Stackblitz (it uses JIT compiler instead of AoT?) so created a separate repo with a minimal reproduction: https://github.com/th0r/ng9-classname-bug Steps: 1. issue.body:
Previously all static styling information (including the ones from component/directive host bindings) would get merged into a single value before it would be written into the `@Input('class'/'style')`. The new behavior specifically excludes host values from the `@Input` bindings.

Fix #35383
